newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BUNGEE-JUMPING COACH PLOTS BAYERN'S FALL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BUNGEE-JUMPING COACH PLOTS BAYERN'S FALL.

text.p: Werner Lorant, the coach of 1860 Munich, proved he is a man willing to take a risk earlier this week by jumping off a Hamburg television tower.
Lorant was performing a bungee jump which will feature in a film to be shown during the half-time break in Sunday's derby match with Bundesliga leaders Bayern Munich.
The coach, who has led 1860 from regional soccer all the way to the Bundesliga, was scarcely back on his own two feet before pledging a similarly daring approach to the 185th Munich derby.
"I'm not scared," Lorant said. "A person who doesn't dare doesn't win."
Lorant and his "Lions", as 1860 are nicknamed, will be taking a leap into the unknown if they manage to beat Bayern.
The club have not defeated their arch rivals since 1977. Since 1860 Munich returned to the Bundesliga in 1994 after years in the wilderness, they have lost four times to Bayern and drawn once.
But that 1-1 draw came in the first half of this season -- a fact which suggests 1860 are constantly improving and it may be only a matter of time before they finally notch up a win.
"We have great respect for 1860," Bayern captain Lothar Matthaeus said. "They've improved their play a lot."
The libero has a high regard for 1860 midfielders such as Polish international Peter Nowak and Ghanaian Abedi Pele.

Matthaeus knows Bayern must win the derby match -- officially a "home" game for 1860 although both sides share the Olympic Stadium -- if they are to be sure of maintaining their three-point cushion over second-placed Bayer Leverkusen.
"We can be champions with four wins and a draw in our last five games," the 1990 World Cup winner said. "But our rivals would be back in touch if we lost and we want to prevent that at all costs."
Leverkusen will draw level on points with Bayern if they beat Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday, piling the pressure on Matthaeus and his team mates for Sunday.

Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni can count on having most of his first-choice players fit but a question mark hangs over midfielder Mario Basler, who is suffering from a thigh strain sustained during Germany's 2-0 win over Ukraine on Wednesday.
Lorant will be able to strengthen the side which won 3-2 against Duisburg last weekend to keep 1860 in the hunt for a UEFA Cup place.

Pele is back from international duty, although not certain of a starting place. Swiss defender Maco Walker is available again after suspension and leading goalscorer Bernhard Winkler may have recovered sufficiently from a groin strain.
